section: VITAMIN D LOADING DETERMINATION BY FTIR-ATR
content: In this research we measured vitamin D levels by means of Fourier transform infra red method in conjugation with the evanescent wave spectroscopy technique, in order to develop a simpler vitamin D measurement method.

title: УПРАВЛЕНИЕ В МЕДИЦИНЕ И БИОЛОГИИ
authors: E. Simanaa, B.Sc., Electrical Engineering, eran.simana@gmail.com
section: VITAMIN D LOADING DETERMINATION BY FTIR-ATR
content: Methods: Blood samples were collected from patients with vitamin D deficiency at five intervals before and up to 16 days after they took a dose of 200,000 IU vitamin D . Samples were measured by the conventional bio-chemical method and by the evanescent wave spectroscopy means. Results: Correlation was found between the vitamin D levels measured by the traditional method and by the evanescent wave spectroscopy technique.

content: A simple metal-free electrochemical immunosensor based on nitrogen-doped graphene acid (NGA) for the detection of 25-hydroxy vitamin D (25-OH D ) is presented.

authors: Jakub Janek1 · Zdenka Fohlerova1,2 · Ivan Dědek3 · Vítězslav Hrubý3 · David Panáček3,4 · Jaromir Hubalek1 ·
content: The use of NGA, with its well-defined chemical composition, high density 3 3 of carboxyl functional groups, and excellent biocompatibility, provided a stable and efficient platform for biomolecule immo- bilization without the need for complex surface modifications.

title: Microchimica Acta (2025) 192:823
authors: Jakub Janek1 · Zdenka Fohlerova1,2 · Ivan Dědek3 · Vítězslav Hrubý3 · David Panáček3,4 · Jaromir Hubalek1 ·
content: The proposed immunosensor demonstrated high sensitivity (1.97 kΩ ng ‒1 mL c m ‒2) and a working range of 3.96 to 48.83 ng mL ‒1, aligning with clinically relevant vitamin D levels. Moreover, the developed immunosensor exhibited excellent specificity, with minimal cross-reactivity and strong resistance to non-specific adsorption. Furthermore, it maintained stable electrochemical performance for up to 30 days, demonstrating its suitability for practical applications.

content: Compared to existing vitamin D sensors, our platform introduces a streamlined fab- rication process that avoids heavy metals, improves reproducibility, and enhances accessibility for point-of-care diagnostics. content: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608 Manuscript_64aa770cf956dd2c2fbd0b422de81fe6 Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues J Christopher Gallagher1, Clifford J Rosen 2 Creighton University Medical School ;2 Maine Medical Center Research Institute, Scarborough, ME, USA. email. jcg@creighton.edu History of discovery of vitamin D and recent discoveries in vitamin D metabolism (Panel) Rickets been recognized for hundreds of years. In 1889 a disease map in England showed that rickets occurred in the industrial towns,1 was more noticeable in spring and disappeared in the summer2. In 1919 sunlight and ultraviolet light (UV) were shown to cure rickets.3. In the same year, the British biochemist and nutritionist Edward Mellanby tested multiple diets, including Scottish porridge, to induce rickets in dogs.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: He then cured it with cod liver oil and concluded that cod liver oil contained a fat soluble factor; either vitamin A or something similar.4 A clinical trial published in 1922 in The Lancet showed that childhood rickets could be healed by cod liver oil, ultraviolet light and sunlight exposure and this was attributed to vitamin A.5 In order to see if vitamin A was the active agent McCollum and colleagues in the USA oxidized cod liver oil to destroy vitamin A but found that the oil still cured rickets in rats.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: They hypothesized the presence of a fourth vitamin which they called vitamin D (the next letter in the alphabet). 6 Around the same time, Steenbock and Black conducted a series of experiments in which they irradiated both rats and their food with UV light and found that both procedures prevented rickets, concluding that a lipid in the diet and skin was converted by UV light into an anti -rachitic substance.7 This process was patented and became the foundation for commercial vitamin D supplementation of foods that prevented rickets thereafter.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: This was a momentous discovery and led to widespread vitamin D supplementation 200- 400 IU daily in children in Europe and North America and the elimination of rickets.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: In 1925 Hess and colleagues in New York showed that UV light could convert cholesterol to produce ergosterol. 8 They used this process to treat rickets and showed that one ounce of activated ergosterol was equivalent to 6 tons of cod liver oil, but it was so potent in children that it caused severe hypercalcemia.9 Commercially irradiation of plant ergosterol produced ergocalciferol now named vitamin D210,11 which has been available since 1931 as ‘Vigantol’ and ‘Haliverol’. However, the natural form of vitamin D3 was discovered in 1936 after irradiation of 7 dehydrocholesterol produced vitamin D 12 (). Both vitamin D2 and D3 have been available from the 1930’s to treat rickets, osteomalacia, hypoparathyroidism, and renal bone disease. Later experiments showed vitamin D2 and D3 were not biologically active but had to be converted to more active metabolites.

content: The first metabolite discovered in 1968 was 25 hydroxyvitamin D (25OHD) 13 but the slow increase in calcium absorption suggested that there must be another active metabolite. In 1971, the active metabolite, produced in the kidney was identified as 1,25 dihydroxyvitamin D3 (1,25(OH) D).14- 16 In 1974, synthetic 1,25 dihydroxyvitamin D3 (calcitriol) became available for clinical use in renal bone disease, hypoparathyroidism and osteoporosis17. (Panel) Vitamin D metabolism.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: It is now understood that 1,25 dihydroxyvitamin D3 is also a hormone and levels are homeostatically regulated by both parathyroid hormone (PTH)18,19 via changes in serum calcium and fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) via changes in serum phosphate.20 Both PTH and FGF 23 are involved in feedback regulation of 1,25 dihydroxyvitamin D secretion, PTH stimulating formation of the hormone and FGF 23 suppressing it while 1,25 dihydroxyvitamin D3 suppresses PTH and stimulates FGF23.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: Initially 1,25 dihydroxyvitamin D was thought to regulate only mineral homeostasis but in the 1970’s 1,25 dihydroxyvitamin D was found to bind to a receptor (VDR) present in many tissues and stimulate transcription of several hundred genes 21,22These cells have the same enzymatic system as the kidney and can convert 25OHD to active 1,25 dihydroxyvitamin D and non-active 24,24(OH)2D. Measurement of vitamin D metabolites.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: Vitamin D3 entering the blood via skin synthesis or from diet has a half-life of 12 hours 23; 25OHD has a half-life of about 2 weeks 24and serum 1,25 dihydroxyvitamin D has a half-life of 4-6 hours.25 Because serum 1,25 dihydroxyvitamin D3 is a hormone whose levels remain constant it is not a useful measurement for assessing vitamin D status in normal people although the level is usually low in chronic renal failure when the kidney fails to synthesize it. Measuring serum 25OHD is ideal because of its longer half-life and it is a biomarker of vitamin D exposure from sunlight and diet.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: Using assays for serum 25OHD, studies from 1975 in northern Europe showed evidence of extensive severe vitamin D deficiency,40 percent of people in UK had levels less than 25nmol/L (10ng/ml),26,27 in Ireland and France 50 percent of nursing homes residents had levels less than10nmol/L(4 ng/ml), 28,29 and in Holland 79 % of nursing home patients had levels less than 25nmol/L (12ng/ml)that increased to normal with vitamin D treatment.30 Possible reasons for such low levels in Northern Europe are the lack of adequate sunlight, especially in the winter months, and absence of dietary supplementation. Today the recommended lower normal range for serum 25OHD is 50nmol/L (20 ng/ml).

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: To circumvent technical issues with measurement of serum 25OHD, which varies by 20-30 percent across multiple assay systems, the recent introduction of calibration standards now used by many companies, allows comparisons amongst studies. 31 Controversies surrounding determination of the vitamin D recommended dietary allowance The IOM (Institute of Medicine-now National Academy of Medicine) convened a committee to study available data on Vitamin D and chronic diseases.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: Their conclusions were that studies of vitamin D, calcium or the combination on health outcomes were inconsistent and it was not possible to synthesize a dose-response related to health outcomes.32 In order to estimate the RDA for vitamin D, a marker or indicator was needed. Because evidence was lacking for a clinical effect of vitamin D on any system other than that of musculoskeletal health this became the indicator for determining RDA.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: There were several lines of evidence showing that a serum 25OHD level of greater than 50nmol/L (20ngml) was associated with lower incidence of fractures in several studies,33, with lower serum PTH and normalization of bone turnover markers.33 A meta-analysis of osteoporosis trials showed that vitamin D 800 IU plus 1200mg calcium significantly reduced fractures by 8%,34 although this result was heavily dependent on the inclusion of a large study of French nursing home women, mean age 86 years.35 If a serum 25OHD of 50nmol/l (20ng/ml) was the target then the question was what dose of vitamin D would exceed this level.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: A meta regression analysis of all serum 25OHD data collected in wintertime studies in Northern latitudes when UV would have a minimal effect on vitamin D synthesis in skin showed that vitamin D 600 IU would meet a serum 25OHD of 50nmol/L in 97.5 % of the population, so the RDA was set at 600 IU for most adults.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: Because of lack of knowledge about vitamin D metabolism in older people, the presence of comorbidities, uncertainty about their diet, sun exposure, the RDA for elderly was increased to 800 IU32. The proposed RDA immediately aroused controversy and many in the clinical bone and mineral field disagreed and thought the RDA was too low.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: Later that year, the Endocrine Society published clinical practice guidelines that contrasted sharply with the IOM; they recommended that a normal serum 25OHD level was 75nmol/L (30ng/ml), values between 50-75nmol/L (20-30ng/ml) indicated vitamin D ‘insufficiency’ and levels less than 50nmol/L (20ng/ml) represented vitamin D deficiency.36 To meet the Endocrine Society target of 75nmol/L (30ng/ml) people were advised to take vitamin D 1,500-2,000 IU daily and up to 10,000 IU/d to correct vitamin D deficiency.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: As a further recommendation, the Endocrine society strongly suggested that increasing vitamin D levels higher than the American IOM recommendation might also reduce the incidence of numerous extra skeletal diseases including cancer, heart disease, falls, and depression.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: These guidelines blurred the distinction between population guidelines, 600-800 IU daily outlined by the IOM, and prevention of extra skeletal disease that may need higher doses of vitamin D, but for which there were no clinical trial data. As such, it was an experimental recommendation.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: Although the Endocrine Society did not directly recommend population testing in their guidelines, publicity in social media caused increased demand for vitamin D tests.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: Recommended levels of serum 25OHD escalated, as more association papers suggested that optimal 25OHD levels of 100-200nmol/L (40- 80 ng/ml) could reduce cancer, immune disorders and cardiovascular disease and hence would require a total daily vitamin D input from 3,000 to 9,6,00 IU.37,38 Despite the widespread criticism of the IOM recommendation of 600 IU and a target serum 25OHD of 50nmol/L, similar recommendations using the same indicator of musculoskeletal health were formulated by many other national committees; e.g. 400 IU in the UK 39 ,600 IU by the European Food and Safety Association40; 800 IU by German Austrian, Swiss societies; 41 400 IU to 70 years and 800 IU after 70 years of age by Nordic and Netherlands societies; 42,43600 IU up to age 70 years and 800 IU after age 70 by Australian and New Zealand Societies.44 Following these two reports 32,36 interest in vitamin D increased exponentially. Because of rapid development of immunoassays for measuring 25OHD there are data from every continent in the world.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: Serum 25OHD levels in all continents show 30-80 percent of the general population have values less than 50nmol/L (20ng/ml) 45-48 except in summer when serum 25OHD often increases above 50nmol/l (20ng/ml) 32 Unexpectedly, countries with high sun exposure such as Morocco, Ethiopia, Saudi Arabia, parts of Spain and Italy have as many as 70% of the population with serum 25OHD less than 50nmol/L (20ng/ml).48 and may have 30-50 percent of people with severe vitamin D deficiency,< 25nmol/L (10ng/ml).49 Immigrants into Western countries are commonly found to have very low serum 25OHD levels; this may be due to cultural habits which includes protective clothing and veils, both of which limit sun exposure.45,50-51 They may also have calcium deficiency rickets.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: In infants and children in Africa where serum 25OHD levels are normal very low calcium intake (less than 200mg/d) is a cause of rickets and calcium 300-500mg/day alone can cure rickets.45,47 It should be noted these studies are not population sampling, but convenience sampling based on clinics or volunteers and marked deficiency may occur in subgroups not tested.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: In contrast Scandinavian countries with long standing policies of vitamin D supplementation have less than 1% of their population with serum 25OHD less than 25nmol/L (10ng/ml)46 The next phase of vitamin D research: The discovery in 1988 that vitamin D receptors and the vitamin D enzyme system exist in most cells in the body inducing transcription of several hundred genes, led to the idea that larger amounts of vitamin D might be beneficial in preventing the onset of non-skeletal diseases such as cancer, heart attacks, depression, chest infection, diabetes52 and other diseases.36,53 As a result, a next phase of clinical vitamin D activity began.

content: Very large trials were initiated in several sites around the world starting around 2005, and since then approximately 100,000 subjects have been entered into controlled randomized trials of placebo/vitamin D. To accommodate large numbers and increase compliance a pragmatic plan often used was to give very large doses (bolus) annually, quarterly, monthly, or weekly.

content: However, in retrospect it would have been wiser to perform feasibility studies on daily versus infrequent bolus doses in view of some unusual results from these trials.

content: Recent results of randomized placebo-controlled trials with vitamin D. Studies of ~ 80,000 participants in randomized vitamin D/placebo-controlled trials did not show a significant reduction in the incidence of fractures, cancer, heart disease, type 2 diabetes, upper respiratory infections, asthma (Table) and tuberculosis. In the table we review the latest trials.

content: Although studies had a defined dose, subjects in both vitamin D and the placebo arms were allowed to continue their own vitamin D supplements and serum 25OHD reflected total vitamin D input. Effect of vitamin D on fracture. (Table). In 10 large prospective placebo-controlled studies of ~57,000 participants, vitamin D was given bolus doses in 5 studies 54-58 and daily in 5 studies 59-63. Subjects were followed up to 5 years.

authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: In 2 bolus studies of large single doses (300,000 IU i.m. and oral 500,000 IU) there were significant increases in hip fractures of 82 percent in women but not men 54. and 26 percent increase in all fractures in women that was attributed to an increase in falls.55 In 5 studies using oral daily doses 400- 2,000 IU there was no effect on fracture incidence.59-63 Serum 25OHD on vitamin D treatment averaged 77nmol/L ( range 55-132 nmol/L (24-50ng/ml) depending on dose compared to placebo 52nmol/l (21ng/ml) Subgroup analysis in 2 studies totally 28,546 subjects 61,63 were not able to show any difference in fracture on vitamin D regarding age, sex, race, BMI, osteoporosis medication, previous fracture history, baseline use of vitamin D, supplemental calcium, baseline serum 25OHD. In the largest study a subgroup of 401 subjects with serum 25OHD < 25nmol/l (10ng/ml) had a lower fracture rate as those with higher levels 63.

content: Vitamin D and Falls. (Table) There have been five large well conducted placebo-controlled trials on ~55,000 subjects lasting between 2-5 years that measured the incidence of falls. 55,64-66 Bolus vitamin D doses varied from a single oral dose 500,000 IU annually55, 100,000 IU monthly 57 or 60,000 monthly 64, and daily doses of 2,000 IU65 and 1,000 IU66. There was no significant difference in the incidence of falls between vitamin D and placebo groups. Serum 25OHD on vitamin D averaged 98nmol/L. (39 ng/ml) compared to placebo 67nmol L (27ng/ml). Vitamin D and cancer. (Table). Studies of the effect of vitamin D on cancer incidence were collected on ~36,126 men and women in 5 placebo-controlled studies. Vitamin D doses ranged from bolus 100,000 IU 4 monthly or monthly and 1600 to 2,000 IU daily for up to 5 years.

A recent meta-analysis of 10 studies including the 5 above showed no effect of vitamin D on cancer incidence but did find evidence that vitamin D reduced cancer mortality71; the mechanism for this effect is unknown and may be related to an effect of vitamin D on the immune system. content: Effect of vitamin D on Asthma. (Table) There are about 5 million children and 20 million adults with asthma in the USA and African American children who often have low serum 25OHD are particularly susceptible.75 In a study from North America, 200 high risk children with asthma, average age 9 years who were on low dose inhaled corticosteroids were randomized to vitamin D 4,000 IU daily or placebo. There was no difference between groups in the outcome which was ‘time to a severe exacerbation of asthma’, it was 240 days in the vitamin D group and 253 days in placebo group.76 In another trial of 400 adults, average age 40 years, with asthma and on low dose inhaled corticosteroids, patients were randomized to vitamin D, an initial dose of 100,000IU then 4,000 IU daily or placebo and followed for 28 weeks. The incidence rate of exacerbations of asthma was not significantly different, 28% on vitamin D compared to 29% on placebo.77 In a meta-analysis of individual patient data on 955 patients on the effect of vitamin D on exacerbations of asthmatics needing systemic steroids, there was an overall reduction in events RR 0.74 (0.56-0.97). A subgroup analysis of those with serum 25OHD < 25nmol/l showed a larger effect with RR of 0.33 (0.11-0.98), p=0.046.78 A post hoc analysis of the New Zealand cardiovascular study of 5110 participants was performed in those that had a history of asthma or COPD; there were 402 cases in the vitamin D and 373 in the placebo groups. There was no significant difference in exacerbations between the two groups, however in the 60 subjects with serum 25OHD levels < 25nmol/l (10ng/ml), exacerbations occurred in 2/27 on vitamin D compared to 23/33 on placebo. (ρ< 0.005)79 Effect of vitamin D on the incidence of respiratory infections. (Table). There have been two large bolus trials. In a study from New Zealand 5,110 adults were randomized to vitamin D, 200,000 IU initially then 100,000 IU monthly or placebo and followed for 3.5 years.

Subgroup analysis showed that benefits were confined to small daily doses 400-1,000 IU and trials lasting less than 12 months (OR 0.78 (0.65-0.94).

The effect of vitamin D in preventing Tuberculosis was performed in a study of 8,551 children in Mongolia, comparing vitamin D3 14,000 IU weekly or placebo for 3 years.83 The primary outcome was a positive test for tuberculosis after 3 years. At the end of study there was no difference between the groups in positive TB tests, 3.6% in the D group and 3.3% in the placebo group. Serum 25OHD at baseline was very low < 30nmol/L (12ng/ml) and the level on vitamin D was 80nmol/L (32ng/ml).

content: Effect of vitamin D on Covid-19. Recently 2 prospective vitamin D placebo controlled trials were completed and the results in both studies were negative for prevention of Covid-19 and upper respiratory infections.85,86 In a study in the UK 3,100 participants were randomized to daily 3200 IU or 800 IU if serum 25OHD < 75nmol/L(30ng/ml) and compared to 3100 controls; the endpoint was a positive covid PCR test and upper respiratory infections after 6 months.

content: There was no difference between treated and untreated.86 Study results may have been influenced by the start of the national covid vaccination program because by the end of study 89% had been vaccinated and a high number took their own vitamin supplements during study perhaps knowing they had low baseline 25OHD levels < 75nmol/L(30ng/ml)85. In the other study in Norway 34,741 subjects were randomized to cod liver oil containing 400 IU vitamin D or none for 6 months. Baseline 25OHD was 70.5nmol/L (28ng/ml) and by end study 67.9nmol/l (27 ng/ml). There was no reduction in positive PCR SARS test or in serious covid infection between groups.86.

content: Effect of Vitamin D on Auto immune diseases. (Table). In the 5 year VITAL trial 25,871 participants the study design was a two by two factorial design testing vitamin D 2000 IU daily and Omega 3 fatty acids 1g daily or placebo.87 In the vitamin D only arm there was a lower incidence of overall auto immune diseases on vitamin D (n123)compared to placebo (n155), marginally significant; HR 0.78 (0.61-0.99, r = 0.05) If only the last 3 years of the trial were considered then the incidence of auto immune diseases was reduced further HR 0.61;0.43-0.86, p =0.005; this result may support the latency of the treatment effect although other statistical models did not confirm a time effect and this was an unplanned analysis. .

content: Effect of calcium combined with vitamin D on fractures. A recent meta-analysis analyzed fracture data from 7 studies conducted in community dwelling and excluded nursing home studies.88 Treatment with calcium and vitamin D did not significantly decrease any type of fracture compared to placebo or no treatment and subgroup analysis based on calcium/vitamin D dose, baseline calcium intake, serum 25OHD and previous fracture history did not change results. Of note, the new meta-analysis showed no effect of calcium on fractures.

content: This can in part be explained by reanalysis of the original WHI study that initially reported a reduction in hip fractures of 12 percent on calcium (HR 0.88 (0.72-1.08) 89 but the group included 18,176 women on calcium plus hormone treatment and 18,106 on placebo. In a recent latest reanalysis of the WHI study after excluding women on hormones there were 4015 on calcium/vitamin D only (total calcium intake 2100mg daily) and 3957 on placebo, a comparison between these groups showed no effect of calcium on hip fracture incidence [RR 1.20 (0.85-1.69)].90 Thus, present evidence does not support the use of calcium and vitamin D in community living people but whether this applies to people in nursing home or those with very low calcium intake is not known. Safety of vitamin D. Recommendations from agencies evaluating safety of a nutrient set a Tolerable upper limit (TUL) of 4,000 IU daily32.

authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: Previously this recommendation was based on observational case reports of vitamin D intoxication including hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, renal stones, and calcification of arteries.32 It is impossible ethically to conduct a deliberate study of vitamin D intoxication thus we have to rely on case reports from literature and studies performed in animal models; toxicity studies from rats91 show similar findings to those humans including hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria and it has been suggested that 25OHD rather than calcitriol is the cause and findings from case reports suggest doses of 10,000-40,000 IU daily can produce toxicity.32 Because of uncertainty about the small numbers of case reports the TUL of 10,000 IU daily was reduced to 4,000 IU daily for all adults.32 However, the TUL applies to vitamin D only and there is no guidance for when vitamin D combined with calcium but when smaller doses of vitamin D 800-2000 IU are combined with calcium as in the milk alkali or calcium alkali syndromes it can more easily cause vitamin D intoxication and long term renal damage especially in the elderly.92,93 A study of vitamin D doses 400 - 4800 IU combined with a calcium intake of 1200mg /d as recommended by National Osteoporosis Societies produced hypercalciuria in 30 percent of older women.94 The limitations of deriving a TUL are the lack of knowledge about long term adverse effects of high daily doses not associated with classic vitamin D intoxication, although evidence is emerging that even lower daily doses less than 4,000 IU may have adverse effects. The paradigm is shifting.

title: Version of Record: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213858723000608
authors: Vitamin D. 100 years of discoveries yet controversy continues
content: Classic vitamin D intoxication is characterized by hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis.32,91 Recent vitamin D trials, however, report new and unexpected adverse events without signs of vitamin D intoxication; these include increased fractures after annual injections of 300,000 IU 55 and after annual bolus oral doses of 500,000 IU54 .Increased falls after 500,000 annually54; increased injurious falls, hospitalizations and death on daily doses of 1,000 IU 2,000 IU and 4,000 IU/daily.66 An increase in peripheral bone loss after 3 years on daily doses of 4,000 and 10,000IU daily compared to 400 IU daily.96 There are few longitudinal studies of the effect of vitamin D where the primary outcome was time to first fall or death.

For these same outcomes rates were higher on 4,000IU HR1.68(0.86-3.27).66 Notably these events occurred in elderly women average age 77 years. Summary.

content: Method evaluation study of a new generation of vitamin D assays Dietmar Enko*, Gernot Kriegshäuser, Robert Stolba, Elfriede Worf, Gabriele Halwachs-Baumann Institute of Laboratory Medicine, General Hospital Steyr, Steyr, Austria *Corresponding author: dietmar.enko@gespag.at

title: Original papers
authors: Dietmar Enko*, Gernot Kriegshäuser, Robert Stolba, Elfriede Worf, Gabriele Halwachs-Baumann
content: Introduction: Recently several diagnostic manufacturers have launched new 25-hydroxy-vitamin D (25[OH]D) assays, which are aligned to the Na- tional Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Standard Reference Materials (SRM) (NIST, Gaithersburg, Maryland).

title: Original papers
authors: Dietmar Enko*, Gernot Kriegshäuser, Robert Stolba, Elfriede Worf, Gabriele Halwachs-Baumann
content: The aim of this study was to compare the performance of one liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method, one enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and one recalibrated and previous version of a chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA).

title: Original papers
authors: Dietmar Enko*, Gernot Kriegshäuser, Robert Stolba, Elfriede Worf, Gabriele Halwachs-Baumann
content: Material and methods: Serum-aliquots of 198 patient samples from routine 25(OH)D analysis were measured by the ClinMass® LC-MS/MS Com- plete Kit (RECIPE Chemicals + Instruments GmbH, Munich, Germany), the ORGENTEC 25(OH)D/D ELISA (ORGENTEC Diagnostika GmbH, Mainz, Ger- 3 2 many), the recalibrated Immunodiagnostic Systems (IDS)-iSYS 25(OH)DS and the previous used IDS-iSYS 25(OH)D CLIA (Immunodiagnostic Systems Ltd, Boldon, United Kingdom). Bland-Altman and Deming regression analyses were calculated for methods comparison of all tested 25(OH)D assays. The LC-MS/MS method was defined as the reference method. Within-run and between-run precision measurements were performed for all met- hods with three different concentration levels.

title: Original papers
authors: Dietmar Enko*, Gernot Kriegshäuser, Robert Stolba, Elfriede Worf, Gabriele Halwachs-Baumann
content: Results: Compared to the LC-MS/MS method, the new IDS-iSYS 25(OH)DS and ORGENTEC 25(OH)D/D assay demonstrated mean relative biases of 3 2 16.3% and 17.8%. The IDS-iSYS 25(OH)D assay showed the lowest mean bias of 1.5%.

title: Original papers
authors: Dietmar Enko*, Gernot Kriegshäuser, Robert Stolba, Elfriede Worf, Gabriele Halwachs-Baumann
content: Deming regression analyses of the recalibrated IDS-iSYS 25(OH) DS and the ORGENTEC 25(OH)D/D assay showed proportional differences, when compared to the reference method. All assays showed a within-run 3 2 and between-run imprecision of ≤ 20% at each of the evaluated concentration levels. Conclusions: The evaluated standardized immunoassays and LC-MS/MS are useful methods for measuring 25(OH)D serum-levels in clinical labora- tories. Key words: vitamin D; immunoassays; liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry; reference standards; quality improvement

title: Original papers
authors: Fatma Emel Kocak*1, Bahadir Ozturk2, Ozben Ozden Isiklar3, Ozlem Genc4, Ali Unlu2, Irfan Altuntas1
content: In this study, we compared two automated immunoassay methods, the Abbott Architect 25-OH Vitamin D assay and the Roche Cobas Vitamin D total assay, with the liquid chromatography- tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Materials and methods: One hundred venous blood samples were randomly selected from routine vitamin D tests. Two of the serum aliquots were analyzed at the Abbott Architect i2000 and the Roche Cobas 6000’s module e601 in our laboratory within the same day. The other serum aliquots were analyzed at the LC-MS/MS in different laboratory. Passing-Bablok regression analysis and Bland-Altman plot were used to compare methods. Inter-rater agreement was analyzed using kappa (κ) analysis.

title: Original papers
authors: Fatma Emel Kocak*1, Bahadir Ozturk2, Ozben Ozden Isiklar3, Ozlem Genc4, Ali Unlu2, Irfan Altuntas1
content: Results: The Roche assay showed acceptable agreement with the LC-MS/MS based on Passing-Bablok analysis (intercept: -5.23 nmol/L, 95% CI: -8.73 to 0.19; slope: 0.97, 95% CI: 0.77 to 1.15). The Abbott assay showed proportional (slope: 0.77, 95% CI: 0.67 to 0.85) and constant differences (intercept: 17.08 nmol/L; 95% CI: 12.98 to 21.39). A mean bias of 15.1% was observed for the Abbott and a mean bias of -14.1% was observed for the Roche based on the Bland-Altman plots.

title: Original papers
authors: Fatma Emel Kocak*1, Bahadir Ozturk2, Ozben Ozden Isiklar3, Ozlem Genc4, Ali Unlu2, Irfan Altuntas1
content: We found strong to nearly perfect agreement in vitamin D status between the immunoassays and LC-MS/ MS. (κ: 0.83 for Abbott, κ: 0.93 for Roche) using kappa analysis.

title: Original papers
authors: Fatma Emel Kocak*1, Bahadir Ozturk2, Ozben Ozden Isiklar3, Ozlem Genc4, Ali Unlu2, Irfan Altuntas1
content: Conclusion: Both immunoassays demonstrated acceptable performance, but the Roche Cobas assay demonstrated better performance than the Abbott Architect in the studied samples.

content: Development of free 25-hydroxyvitamin D assay method using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry NauIshimine1,ShixingWu1,RyuseiOta2,KojiTakahashi3,MasakiTakiwaki3,MitsutoshiSugano4, MinoruTozuka5 and TakeshiUehara1,6 1DepartmentofLaboratoryMedicine,ShinshuUniversityHospital,Matsumoto,Japan;2DivisionofMedicalTechnology,SchoolofHealthSciences,ShinshuUniversitySchoolof Medicine,Matsumoto,Japan;3MedicalEquipmentBusinessOperations,JEOLLtd.,Tokyo,Japan;4DepartmentofClinicalLaboratorySciences,SchoolofHealthSciences, FukushimaMedicalUniversity,Fukushima,Japan;5LifeScienceResearchCenter,NaganoChildren’sHospital,Azumino,Japan;6DepartmentofLaboratoryMedicine,Shinshu UniversitySchoolofMedicine,Matsumoto,Japan Correspondence:TakeshiUehara(tuehara@shinshu-u.ac.jp) Thefreehormonehypothesishastriggeredcontroversiesregardingthemeasurementoffree vitaminDmetabolites,suchasfree25-hydroxyvitaminD(25(OH)D),asasuitableindicator fortotalvitaminDforclinicaluse.Thisissuecanbeaddressedbydevelopingapreciseand accuratemethodforfree25(OH)Dmeasurement.Inthepresentstudy,anovelassaymethod forfree25(OH)D basedonliquidchromatography-tandemmassspectrometry(LC-MS/MS) wasdeveloped.SamplepreparationfirstinvolvedultrafiltrationtoremovevitaminD-binding protein-boundandalbumin-bound25(OH)D,followedbyextractionwithacolumn,derivati- zation,evaporation,dissolution,andinjectionintotheLC-MS/MSsystem.Thecoefficientof variationofrepeatabilityandreproducibilityobtainedwere3.8–4.5%and4.8–5.9%,respec- tively.Satisfactorylinearity(r=0.999)wasobtainedupto80pg/ml.Thelowerquantification limitwas0.97pg/mlandtheS/Nratioonthepeakof1.0pg/mlsamplewas24.8(whichis morethantheacceptablevalueof10).Therecoveryratewasbetween84.5and92.4%with a negligible matrix effect (94.5–104.9%).

content: However, the present immunoassays measure total 25(OH)D levels and cross-react with other vita- minDmetabolitessuchas24,25-dihydroxyvitaminD (24,25(OH) D )[10].Recently,somemethodsusingliquid 3 2 3 chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) for measuring vitamin D concentrations have been re- ported[11–14].Allofthesemethodswerecarriedoutsimilarly:additionofinternalstandard,extraction,derivatiza- tion,anddetection.However,eachmethodhasapeculiaringenuitysuchastheuseofdriedbloodspotsasasample [11], one-step estimate of bioavailable vitamin D and vitamin D metabolite ratio [12], serum sample preparation usingproteinprecipitation[13],andhigh-throughputmethod[14].TheadvantageoftheLC-MS/MSmethodsfor detectionofvitaminDistheabilityoftheproceduretosimultaneouslymeasuremultiplevitaminDmetabolites,such as25(OH)D ,3-epi-25-hydroxyvitaminD (3-epi-25(OH)D ),24,25(OH) D ,1α,25(OH) D ,and25(OH)D . 3 3 3 2 3 2 3 2 The free hormone hypothesis [15,16] is a proposition that the free fraction of hormones (i.e., unbound to any protein)canaccessmosttargetcellcytoplasmbydiffusionandexpressbiologicaleffects.Thefreefractionratiovaries greatlydepending onthehormone.Forexample, theratiooffreethyroxineis0.03%, whilethatoffreecortisolis 4–10% [16]. title: CDC Vitamin D Standardization-Certification Program (CDC VDSCP)
authors: Certified Total 25-hydroxyvitamin D Assays
content: See https://www.cdc.gov/clinical-standardization-programs/media/pdfs/2024/04/CDC-Certified-Vitamin-D-Procedures-508.pdf for previous list of certified assays. • The following assays have successfully met the performance criterion of ±5.0% mean bias when compared to the CDC reference measurement procedure and an overall imprecision of <10%. Only data for total 25-hydroxyvitamin D was used for certification. • It is not the intent of the CDC VDSCP to certify each lot of reagents.

authors: Certified Total 25-hydroxyvitamin D Assays
content: Participants are awarded certificates for successfully meeting bias and imprecision criteria using specific methods that consist of different reagent and calibrator lots. • Analytical performance in the CDC VDSCP is assessed using human serum.

title: CDC Vitamin D Standardization-Certification Program (CDC VDSCP)
authors: Certified Total 25-hydroxyvitamin D Assays
content: Each table includes information about certified assays including participant name, measurement principle, assay identifier, certification measurement range, certification date, individual samples pass rate and contact information. “Assay identifier” is an internal code used by the participant to represent the assay used for certification. “Assay Measurement range” is the assay’s reported analytical measurement range (AMR) and is not the certification range. “Certification Measurement Range” is the concentration range the of the samples used for VDSCP certification. “Certification date” includes historical certification information and gaps between years do not always indicate the assay’s failure to meet certification criteria. “Individual samples pass rate” is the percentage of individual samples out of the 40 provided that met certification criteria of ±5% bias. This information was provided starting February 2017. Note: The ±5% mean bias used for certification can be considered the allowable calibration bias. Certification indicates that the assay is calibrated to meet those limits. Due to differences in test selectivity, measurements on individual samples can exceed the calibration bias. Therefore, the individual sample pass rate provides some information about the selectivity of a test that meets the calibration criteria. Page 1 of 33 Table 1: Currently Certified Assays

content: MicroNIR/Chemometric RobertaRisoluti,GiuseppinaGullifaandStefanoMaterazi* DepartmentofChemistry,SapienzaUniversityofRome,Rome,Italy In this work, an innovative screening platform based on MicroNIR and chemometrics is proposed for the on-site and contactless monitoring of the quality of milk using simultaneous multicomponent analysis.

title: ORIGINALRESEARCH
authors: Assessing the Quality of Milk Using a
content: The novelty of this completely automated tool consists of a miniaturized NIR spectrometer operating in a wireless mode that allows samples to be processed in a rapid and accurate way and to obtain in a single click a comprehensive characterization of the chemical composition of milk. To optimize the platform, milk specimens with different origins and compositions were considered and

title: ORIGINALRESEARCH

Background:TheinterestinvitaminDmeasurementhasstronglyincreasedinrecentyears.Thebestindicatorforcirculating
vitaminDlevelsis25-hydroxy-vitaminD(25(OH)D)whichisoftenmeasuredbydifferentimmunoassays.Wedemonstrate
problems in comparability of measures by different immunoassays and the need for standardization in the context of a
large population-based cohortstudy.
Methods:25(OH)DwasmeasuredwiththeimmunoassaysDiasorinLiaisonin2006in5,386womenandinthecontextof
anotherprojectwithIDS-iSYSin4,199menin2009–2010(whentheDiasorinLiaisonwasnolongeravailableintheversion
utilizedin2006).Standardizationwasperformedbyre-measuringof25(OH)Dlevelsin97menand97womenwithliquid
chromatography tandem-massspectrometry (LC-MS/MS)to obtain linearregression conversion equations.
Results:Applyinga30nmol/Lcut-offvalueforvitaminDdeficiencywouldhaveresultedin48.3%ofwomenand12.1%of
men with vitamin D deficiency ahead of standardization. The large gender difference was strongly attenuated after
standardizationoftheassayswithonly15.7%ofwomenand14.3%ofmenwithvitaminDdeficiency.Standardizationon
averageincreased the25(OH)D levels by 10.3nmol/L inwomenand decreased 25(OH)D levels by2.9nmol/L inmen.
Conclusion:The standardization with LC-MS/MS revealed that much of the observed gender difference was only assay-
driven and the extremely high proportion of 48.3% vitamin D deficient women proved to be an exaggeration of the old
version of the Diasorin-Liaison immunoassay. Standardization of 25(OH)D immunoassay results by LC-MS/MS is
recommendedtoimprovetheiraccuracyandcomparability,providedtheLC-MS/MSmethoditselfisadequatelyvalidated
and standardized. |

authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
section: A R T I C L E I N F O A B S T R A C T
content: Keywords: Objectives: the different analytical methods for measurement of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25 25(OH)Vitamin D (OH)D) are not yet fully harmonized and no consensus exists on a threshold of 25(OH)D defining Method comparison a deficiency status. In this study, we compared the results from the assays of serum 25(OH)D

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: performed with three different methods to evaluate the presence of potential biases and how much these biases can influence the assignment of patients to specific 25(OH)D deficiency/suf- ficiency categories.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Design and Methods: Liaison 25(OH) Vitamin D Total (DiaSorin Liaison XL), Elecsys Vitamin D Total II (Roche Elecsys) and Lumipulse G25(OH) Vitamin D (Fujirebio Lumi- pulse G1200) were used.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Methods comparability was established performing Passing-Bablok regression and Bland-Altman analysis to prove whether the differences found were lower than the preliminarily pre-established maximum acceptable bias. Results: all Passing-Bablok re- gressions exhibited the presence of a proportional and constant systematic error. Bland-Altman analysis revealed biases well above the maximum acceptable bias, so the 25(OH)D concentra- tions measured were not comparable.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: To evaluate whether the three methods had the same ability to classify patients into different categories of vitamin D levels, we categorized results obtained by each method in reference classes.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Lumipulse categorized most patients into the class with the lowest 25(OH)D concentrations (<20 ng/mL) whereas Elecsys ranked the lowest number. Con- clusions: Liaison XL and Elecsys have shown good accuracy compared to Lumipulse in measuring 25(OH)D levels.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Nevertheless, the assays were not interchangeable due to the lack of compara- bility of results as well as to the disagreement in classification of hormone deficiency or sufficiency. * Corresponding author. ** Corresponding author. title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Vitamin D has a pivotal role in calcium metabolism and in the preservation of skeletal health and it is associated with several human disorders, including cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and infectious diseases, among others [1–4].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The international scientific community recognizes the measurement of 25 OH total Vitamin D (25(OH)D) as the best parameter to evaluate the reserves of this hormone [5,6]. The 25(OH)D deficiency is spread worldwide [7] and the routine assessment of 25(OH)D status in patients has grown exponentially in recent years [8]. The clinical laboratory may use either mass spectrometry (HPLC/MSMS) or immunometric methods to assay serum levels of 25 (OH)D [6]. However, the different analytical methods are not yet fully harmonized [9]. To date, in fact, despite technological in- novations and its complete automation, the assay of 25(OH)D represents a challenge for the laboratory.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The analytical inaccuracy is mainly due to the existence of different forms of 25(OH)D with similar biological activity and to the lipophilic nature of these mol- ecules, as well as to the presence of various metabolic interferents and epimers [10]. Furthermore, 25(OH)D can be transported both from the Vitamin D Binding Protein (VDBP) and from albumin and lipoproteins. The concentration of these 25(OH)D binding proteins varies according to pathophysiological conditions of the organism, such as pregnancy or kidney disease.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Moreover, 25(OH)D binds these proteins with different affinity constants and must be separated from them before the execution of the measurement, therefore introducing a further variable on 25(OH)D determination [10].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: To address the lack of assays standardization, in 2010 several national and international organizations, together with the Office of Dietary Supplements (ODS) of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), have organized the Vitamin D Standardization Program (VDSP) aimed to: i) identify HPLC/MSMS as the reference procedure measurement; ii) provide reference sera to the manufacturers of analytical assays to calibrate their commercial systems; and, iii) promote two external quality assessment programs based on accuracy [11,12].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Within the VDSP, the US Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) also certifies and publishes annually the list of manufacturers whose analytical method has successfully met the requirements for standardization [13]. However, although the accuracy of the various analytical methods has improved, much work remains to be done [10,14,15].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Numerous studies of automated immunoassays comparison demonstrated how, despite the excellent correlation with the reference procedure made them valid for the 25(OH)D measurement in the routine clinical laboratory, the incomplete standardization resulted in significant bias when the methods were compared to each other [15–17].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The significant variability in 25(OH)D measure obtained by different methods has also complicated the definition of a universal deficiency threshold for 25(OH)D [10,18]. Currently, in fact, no universal consensus exists on threshold of 25(OH)D defining a vitamin D deficiency status.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The US Institute of Medicine (IOM), on the basis of predefined outcomes of mineral metabolism and bone health, recommends a serum 25(OH)D concentration of 20 ng/mL, while the Endocrine Society, after a deep systemic review of literature, proposes a 30 ng/ml concentration as threshold. Essentially, one cause of the controversial threshold could be the lack of vitamin D methods standardization [5,19].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: This study describes the comparison of the results obtained by measurement of serum concentration of 25(OH)D performed with three different tests: Liaison 25(OH) Vitamin D Total test (DiaSorin Liaison XL) (DiaSorin, Saluggia, Italy), Elecsys Vitamin D Total II test (Roche Elecsys) (Roche Diagnostics Gmbh, Mannheim, Germany), and Lumipulse G 25OH Vitamin D test (Fujirebio Lumipulse G1200) (Fujirebio inc, Tokyo, Japan).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The aim of study was: i) evaluate the presence of a potential bias among the different methods and ii) how much this bias can influence the assignment of patients to the specific 25(OH)D deficiency/sufficiency categories.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Within a week, 250 serum samples were analysed for the 25(OH)D concentration by DiaSorin Liaison XL (DiaSorin, Saluggia, Italia) at Clinical Biochemistry Laboratory of Mater Domini University Hospital (Catanzaro, Italy) in February 2020, as part of daily work routine. A total of 51 samples, ranging of serum 25(OH)D concentrations from 4.0 to 103.0 ng/mL, were selected, anonymized, ali- quoted into 2 tubes and 25(OH)D concentration assayed by Roche Elecsys and Fujirebio Lumipulse G1200 tests. Ethical approval was not required because the samples are anonymized before to be subjected to further analysis.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The study was conducted according to Helsinki declaration on human experimentation. 2.2. 25(OH)D methods The 25(OH)D (ng/ml) determinations were performed with the following automated immunoassays: Liaison 25(OH) Vitamin D Total assay (DiaSorin, Saluggia Italy; lot 134858B); Elecsys Vitamin D Total II test (Roche Diagnostics, Mannheim, Germany; lot 424,995), and Lumipulse G 25OH Vitamin D test (Fujirebio Inc., Tokyo, Japan; lot 8XX0074). All three methods are CDC certified [13].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: DiaSorin Liaison XL is a competitive chemiluminescent immunoassay (CLIA) and Roche Elecsys is based on a competing protein- binding assay for 25(OH)D and uses electro chemiluminescent detection (ECLIA). Finally, Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 is a two-step non-competitive sandwich assay based on chemiluminescent enzyme immunoassay (CLEIA). The 25(OH)D measurement range was 4–150 ng/ml for DiaSorin Liaison XL and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 tests and 3–100 ng/ml for Roche Elecsys test.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: As reported by manufactures, the 25 OH Vitamin D2 and 25 OH Vitamin D3 cross reactivity is equal to 100 % for DiaSorin Liaison XL whereas of 97 % and 100 % for Roche Elecsys, respectively. No data were reported for Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200. All 25(OH)D measurements were performed according to the manufacturer’s instructions in our laboratory. F. Trimboli et al. title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Imprecision for each method was carried out according to the classic 3 ×5 scheme during the routine analytic session [20]. The quality control sera, provided by respective manufacturers, were used to calculate imprecision as coefficient of variation (CV%).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Briefly, for each method, two levels of internal quality control serum were determined in triplicate (at the beginning, in the middle and at the end of the analytical session) for 5 consecutive days and then was calculated the CV% [21].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The methods comparison was carried out following the operating procedures suggested by documents of Clinical Biochemistry and Clinical Molecular Biology Italian Society SiBioC [20,22].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: In particular, each method was compared with other methods by Bland-Altman analysis to verify if the maximum bias was minor the maximum acceptable error (Tea%), that for 25OH(D) is 25 % [23].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Briefly, the maximum acceptable bias was calculated according to the following formula: bias max % =TEa% - 1.65 CVa where CVa is the highest analytical imprecision within the laboratory expressed in % and calculated using the precision control sera.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The accuracy of DiaSorin Liaison XL, Roche Elecsys, and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 methods was evaluated using 10 International Vitamin D External Quality Assessment Scheme (DEQAS) control sera. DEQAS is an external quality control scheme “accuracy based”. The “true” value of 25(OH)D in DEQAS samples were assigned using the LC–MS/MS assay, the Reference Measurement Procedure (RMP) for 25(OH)D measurement. Then, the accuracy of the participants’ results is assessed verifying how far they deviates from the true value indicated by DEQAS program. The biases among results obtained with the three methods were calculated and then compared with the limit threshold of 25 % proposed by the organizer [24,25].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The mean, CV, variance, standard deviation, Passing Bablok regression and Bland-Altman analysis were calculated by MetComp software module vers. 1.0 [20].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: To assess whether DiaSorin Liaison XL, Roche Elecsys, and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 methods homogeneously classified the patients in the 25(OH)D deficiency/sufficiency categories, the Cohen’s kappa coefficient, a measure of the strength of the agreement between methods, was calculated [26].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The values obtained were evaluated according to this scheme: • if κ assumes values between 0.01 and 0.40, the concordance is poor. • if κ assumes values between 0.41 and 0.60, the concordance is fair. • if κ assumes values between 0.61 and 0.80, the concordance is good. • if κ assumes values between 0.81 and 1.00, the concordance is very good.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The precision of DiaSorin Liaison XL, Roche Elecsys, and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 methods was calculated as intra-laboratory CV according to 3 ×5 scheme (Table 1).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: All methods showed a CV% falling within the limits of acceptability declared by manufac- turers: 9.8 %, 7.2 %, and 6 % for DiaSorin Liaison XL, Roche Elecsys, and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200, respectively. The only exception was Roche Elecsys control serum level 1 with a CV =11.41 % (Table 1).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Relationship and agreement among the three methods were performed by comparing them two by two using the Passing - Bablok regression and the Bland – Altman analysis to verify whether the differences between the sample values were below a pre-established beforehand maximum deviation limit, the “maximum acceptable bias” (Bias max).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The formula: Bias max =TEa % - 1.65 CVa was used to calculate the Bias max, where TEa is the total allowable error and CVa the coefficient of variation that express the within-laboratory analytical inaccuracy calculated using precision control sera as reported above.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Starting from the total acceptable error (TEa%) that for vitamin D, based on the evidence in the literature [23] is 25 %, and choosing the CVa with the highest value among those obtained with precision tests, we calculated 1.65 CVa max that is 11.41 ×1.65 =18.83 %. Consequently, the bias max % that not to be exceeded was: 25 % –18.83 % =6.17%.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: First, the 25(OH)D results obtained by DiaSorin Liaison XL were compared with those obtained by Roche Elecsys and then Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200, respectively.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Moreover, the Passing - Bablok regression and the Bland - Altman analyses were applied also to results obtained by Roche Elecsys and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200. 3.2.1.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: DiaSorin Liaison XL vs Roche Elecsys The Passing - Bablok regression between DiaSorin Liaison XL and Roche Elecsys exhibited a linear relation (y =1.4924 +1.1592 x; 95 % C.I. intercept =(cid:0) 0.41 to 4.55; 95 % C.I. slope =1.26 to 1.03 p >0.05) (Fig. 1A) and the presence of a proportional systematic error. The results of Bland-Altman analysis are shown in Fig. 1B.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The mean difference ±standard deviation of 25(OH)D was (cid:0) 6.16 ± 8.12 ng/mL (95 % CI =(cid:0) 8.49 to (cid:0) 3.83) and the limits of agreement carried out were (cid:0) 22.24 to +9.91 ng/mL (Fig. 1B).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The analysis of Bland - Altman on percentage differences showed a mean percentage difference or bias% equal to (cid:0) 22.5 % (95 % C.I. =(cid:0) 29.0 % to (cid:0) 16.0 %) (Fig. 1C).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Since the previously calculated maximum acceptable bias between the methods (6.17 %) was less than the absolute lower limit value of 95 % C.I. bias%, the results provided by DiaSorin Liaison XL and Roche Elecsys were not comparable. 3.2.2.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: DiaSorin Liaison XL vs Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 The Passing - Bablok regression analysis between DiaSorin Liaison XL and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 showed a close relation (y = (cid:0) 1.0894 +0.922 x; 95 % C.I. intercept =-2.48 to 0.05; 95 % C.I. slope =0.87 to 0.98; p >0.05) (Fig. 2A) but both proportional and constant systematic error was present.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Moreover, Bland – Altman analysis revealed a mean difference ±standard deviation of 25(OH)D equal to 3.67 ±4.53 ng/mL (95 % CI =2.39 to 4.35) and the limits of agreement carried out were (cid:0) 5.25 to 12.59 ng/mL (Fig. 2B) whereas the mean bias% was 16.2 % (95 % C.I. bias% =12.01 % to 20.35 %) (Fig. 2C) above the maximum acceptable bias so the 25 (OH)D concentration measured with DiaSorin Liaison XL and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 are not comparable. 3.2.3.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Roche Elecsys vs Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 The Passing - Bablok regression between Roche Elecsys and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 showed a proportional and constant systematic error even in the presence of a good relation (y =(cid:0) 2.7262 +0.8224 x; 95 % C.I. intercept =(cid:0) 4.10 to (cid:0) 1.67; 95 % C.I. slope =0.77 to 0.87; p >0.05) (Fig. 3A).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Moreover, Bland – Altman analysis revealed a mean difference ±standard deviation of 25(OH)D equal to 9.45 ±7.20 ng/mL (95 % CI =7.38 to 11.51) and the limits of agreement carried out were (cid:0) 4.80 to 23.70 ng/mL (Fig. 3B).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The mean bias% was 38.2 % (95 % C.I. bias% =32.47 % to 43.93 %) (Fig. 3C) well above the maximum acceptable bias (6.17 %) meaning that the 25(OH)D concentration measured with Roche Elecsys and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 were not comparable.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The accuracy was evaluated by determining 25(OH)D concentration in 10 DEQAS sera. Samples 561–565 belong to the DEQAS October 2019 distribution and samples 566–570 were from the DEQAS January 2020 distribution.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The calculation of the bias % between the 25(OH)D “true value” provided by DEQAS and those determined by DiaSorin Liaison XL, Roche Elecsys, and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 methods was performed applying the following formula: [(25(OH)DMETHOD X - 25(OH)DDEQAS)/25(OH)DDEQAS] x 100. Next, the mean bias % was calculated for each method. In Table 2 are reported the target values and the bias obtained.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: DEQAS Advisor Panel considers satisfactory the performances obtained if the mean bias % is less than 25 % at least in 3 of the first 4 samples of each distribution. Since for all three methods the % of bias in at least 3 of the 4 samples of each distribution is less than 25 %, it can therefore be said that all methods have achieved the performance target set by DEQAS program.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: To evaluate whether the three methods had a comparable ability in classifying patients into different categories of vitamin D levels according both to Endocrine Society’s guidelines [5] and IOM study [19], we first categorized the results obtained by each method in a reference class (Tables 3 and 4). According to the Endocrine Society’s, Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 method categorizes most patients into the class with the lower 25 F. Trimboli et al. title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: P r a c t i c a l L a b o r a t o r y M e d i c i n e 26(2021)e00251 Fig. 2. 25(OH)D determination by DiaSorin Liaison XL and Fujirebio Lumipulse G1200. (A) Passing – Bablok regression analysis; (B) Bland - Altman analysis of agreement on absolute values of mean differences (ng/mL) between methods; (C) Bland - Altman analysis of agreement on percentage values of mean differences (%) between methods. (OH)D concentration (<10 ng/mL and 11–20 ng/mL) whereas Roche Elecsys categorizes the smaller number of patients into the same class (Table 3). Conversely, Roche Elecsys categorizes most patients into the 21–29 ng/mL and 30–100 ng/mL categories and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 categorizes the smaller number of patients into the same class. According to IOM, Roche Elecsys categorizes the lower number of patients into <20 ng/mL and the higher in >20 ng/mL class and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 vice versa (Table 4).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Finally, we assessed the strength of the agreement between the results obtained with the different methods by calculating Cohen’s κ index, a concordance index that considers the probability that the concordance is random (Table 5).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: When the Endocrine Society’s reference values were used, the strength of the agreement between DiaSorin Liaison XL and Roche Elecsys was very good for each class, except for 11–20 ng/mL category.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: DiaSorin Liaison XL and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 showed a very good agreement only in the lower and the higher 25(OH)D concentration classes, Roche Elecsys and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 only in <10 ng/mL category (Table 5). Conversely, when the IOM reference values were used, the strength of the agreement between DiaSorin Liaison XL and Roche Elecsys and DiaSorin Liaison XL and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 were good whereas between Roche Elecsys and Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 was moderate (Table 6).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The presence of some DEQAS samples with % of bias >25 % (the cut-off proposed by DEQAS program for accuracy) makes fair the Fujirebio Lumipulse G 1200 test performance, but the other two methods show good performance fullfilling the criteria of DEQAS external quality control scheme “accuracy based”.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: This could be explained with the presence in DEQAS samples of metabolites of vitamin D as 25(OH)D2, 3-epi-25-hydroxyvitamin D and 24,25-dihydroxyvitamin D that could influence 25(OH)D determination [25].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Despite the fact that the three tests are accurate, they are not interchangeable as demonstrated by the lack of comparability between the results obtained by the single method. A possible explanation could be that the three analytical procedures measure 25(OH)D concentration with different mechanisms. The Roche Elecsys and Liaison methods are competitive immunoassays while the Lumipulse test is non-competitive.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The Elecsys test is an electrochemiluminescent binding assay in which the labelled 25(OH)D competes with the native for binding to a recombinant VDBP; the DiaSorin method is a chemiluminescent assay in which the labelled 25(OH)D competes with the sample’s 25(OH)D for antibody binding.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Finally, the Lumipulse method, in turn, is a non-competitive chemiluminescence assay in which the sandwich is formed between a capture antibody for 25(OH)D and a second labelled monoclonal antibody directed against the immunocomplex 25 (OH)D - first antibody.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: These are therefore different methods which overlap only partially even if are traceable to the same standard (Standard Reference Material (SRM) 972, National Institute of Standard and Tecnology (NIST)).

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The standardization effort carried out by the Vitamin D Standardization Program should have overcome the differences in the design of the analytical procedures [11,12]. As several authors have pointed out, however, we are still far from a complete standardization [10,14,15]. The need to maintain the serum 25(OH)D concentrations at acceptable levels is recognized by the scientific community as a public health emergency.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: A complex discussion is underway, aimed at examining the available data on the methods used in determining the concentration of vitamin D and identifying the persistent problems associated with them [27].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: It is now universally accepted that, in the general population without problems of chronic kidney disease, the measurement of 25 (OH)D is the best parameter to evaluate the reserves of the active form of the hormone 1,25 OH vitamin D (1,25(OH)2D) [5,6].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: The 1, 25(OH)2D, with other factors including Parathormone (PTH) and Fibroblast Growth Factor 23 (FGF 23), plays a key role in controlling bone metabolism in the human body while maintaining the homeostasis of calcium and phosphorus.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Therefore, vitamin D directly influences the mineral density of bone, and its determination can provide important indications on the risk of falls and fractures [28–31]. Several studies have confirmed the diagnostic importance of vitamin D concentration in diseases affecting bone metabolism. In recent years, numerous experimental and clinical studies have evaluated, with mixed results, the influence of vitamin D deficiency in disorders such as diabetes and cardiovascular, oncological and autoimmune diseases [32–36].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: Furthermore, the role of 25 (OH)D in viral infection has recently been clarified [37] and the use of vitamin D as a possible adjuvant therapy to fight infections such as SARS Covid-2 has been proposed [38–40].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: In fact, there are studies showing that 25(OH)D counteracts viral replication of rotavirus both in vitro and in vivo [41] and that supplementation with 4000 IU/day of vitamin D reduces dengue virus infection [42].

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: On the other hand, it has been shown that 25(OH)D deficiency correlates with increased levels of IL-6, a marker of inflammation infection associated with dysregulated production of hematopoietic cells in patients with HIV [43]. Taken together, these findings have led to an exponential increase in vitamin D determinations. Efforts in the future to improve the standardization policy of the immunoassays will be required.

title: PracticalLaboratoryMedicine26(2021)e00251
authors: Practical Laboratory Medicine
content: If successful, it will allow us to use the same values of cut off and to recognize with the same effectiveness the subjects deficient and those with sufficient 25(OH)D. F. Trimboli et al. P r a c t i c a l L a b o r a t o r y M e d i c i n e 26(2021)e00251 F. Trimboli et al.

content: Two out of three compared immunoassays have shown good accuracy and therefore can be considered as reliable in measuring the 25(OH)D in the routine clinical laboratory. Nevertheless, we showed that the assays are not interchangeable due the lack of comparability of the results. Moreover, these three immunological tests do not agree in classifying patients with either the method proposed by the Endocrine Society or the IOM.

content: Characterization of vitamin D3 biotransformation by the cell lysate of Actinomyces hyovaginalis CCASU-A11-2 Ahmad M. Abbas1,2, Walid F. Elkhatib1,3 , Mohammad M. Aboulwafa1,2, Nadia A. Hassouna1 and Khaled M. Aboshanab1*

title: Abbas et al. AMB Express (2024) 14:43 AMB Express
authors: ORIGINAL ARTICLE Open Access
content: A former work conducted in our Lab, lead to in a effective scale up of vitamin D3 bioconversion into calcitriol by Actinomyces (A.) hyovaginalis isolate CCASU-A11-2 in Lab fermenter (14 L) resulting in 32.8 µg/100 mL of calcitriol. However, the time needed for such a bioconversion process was up to 5 days.

title: Abbas et al. AMB Express (2024) 14:43 AMB Express
authors: ORIGINAL ARTICLE Open Access
content: Therefore, the objective of this study was to shorten the bioconversion time by using cell-free lysate and studying different factors influencing bioconversion.

title: Abbas et al. AMB Express (2024) 14:43 AMB Express
authors: ORIGINAL ARTICLE Open Access
content: The crude cell lysate was prepared, freeze-dried, and primarily fractionated into nine fractions, of which, only three fractions, 50, 100, and 150 mM NaCl elution buffers showed 22, 12, and 2 µg/10 mL, calcitriol production, respectively. Ammonium sulfate was used for protein precipitation, and it did not affect the bioconversion process except at a concentration of 10%w/v.

title: Abbas et al. AMB Express (2024) 14:43 AMB Express
authors: ORIGINAL ARTICLE Open Access
content: Secondary fractionation was carried out using 80 mL of the 50 mM NaCl elution buffer and the results showed the 80 mL eluent volume was enough for the complete elution of the active protein. The pH 7.8, temperature 28 °C, and 6 h reaction time were optimum for maximum calcitriol production (31 µg/10 mL). In conclusion, the transformation of vitamin D3 into calcitriol was successfully carried out within 6 h and at pH 7.8 and 28 °C using fractionated cell lysate. This process resulted in a 10-fold increase in calcitriol as compared to that produced in our previous study using a 14 L fermenter (32.8 µg/100 mL). Therefore, cell-free lysate should be considered for industrial and scaling up vitamin D3 bioconversion into calcitriol.

title: Abbas et al. AMB Express (2024) 14:43 AMB Express
authors: ORIGINAL ARTICLE Open Access
content: Biotransformation of vitamin D into calcitriol has been achieved within 6 h using a cell-free lysate of A. hyovaginalis isolate CCASU-A11-2. pH 7.8 and incubation temperatures 28 °C were optimum for maximum calcitriol production using the cell-free lysate. This study results in a 10-fold (31 µL/10 mL) to that obtained using a 14 L Lab fermenter. Bioconversion using cell-free lysate should be considered for industrial production of calcitriol.

They also contain a range of micronutrients such as vitamin E, some of the B vitamins, sodium, magnesium, and zinc. Because of fortification of some cereal products they also contribute significant amounts of calcium and iron.

content: There is evidence to suggest that regular con- sumption of cereals, specifically whole grains, may have a role in the prevention of chronic diseases (e.g., coronary heart disease and diabetes). A series of works have recently been conducted on the application of NIR spectros- copy to determine nutritional compounds in cereal foods. These works have resulted in a number of rapid online measurement tools with a great potential to be introduced in the cereal processing industry.

The coefficient of determination was 0.89 to 0.97 depending on the samples studied.

Determination of fat in cereal foods using NIR spectroscopy has been a subject of several projects undertaken recently. Reflectance spectra at 400–1700 nm of intact cereal foods have been recorded and processed with multivariate analysis tools. Mathematical models derived allowed predicting the fat content of independent validation samples (n = 52) with sufficient accuracy.

Energy balance is an important parameter of human diet along with its nutritional composition. Therefore the energy available in a food should be known to consumers for management of diet. Control over diet energy balance allows decreasing the risk of obesity and chronic diseases related to food. NIR spectroscopy has also been applied to measure energy contained in foods, particularly in cereal products.

Having a strong sensitivity to compounds contained even in trace amounts, which is beyond that of the other tech- niques, fluorescence spectroscopy could be a powerful tool to study nutritional com- ponents in foods. A number of important biologically active components in foods such as lycopene, tocopherols, and CLA could be studied using fluorescence spec- troscopy.

title: Review Article
authors: Sieglinde Zelzer1, Walter Goessler2, Markus Herrmann1
content: Abstract: Liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) is considered the gold standard for the measurement of vitamin D metabolites as it does not suffer from most of the limitations inherent to immunoassays. In addition, LC-MS/MS offers the advantage measuring several metabolites simultaneously. Despite many advantages, LC-MS/MS methods are not free from analytical challenges.

authors: Sieglinde Zelzer1, Walter Goessler2, Markus Herrmann1
content: Aspects such as sample type, protein precipitation, analyte extraction, derivatization, chromatographic separation ionization and capabilities of the mass spectrometer have to be considered carefully. title: Review Article
authors: Sieglinde Zelzer1, Walter Goessler2, Markus Herrmann1
content: While an extensive number of original studies and review articles has addressed the performance of 25(OH)D immunoassays, the analytical challenges regarding the measurement of vitamin D metabolites by LC-MS/MS are not widely known. Therefore, the aim of this review is to provide a comprehensive overview about existing LC-MS/MS methods for the measurement of vitamin D metabolites and their analytical performance.
